newsitem.title: USA: Alaska volcano erupts beneath thick cloud cover.
newsitem.headline: Alaska volcano erupts beneath thick cloud cover.

text.p: Alaska's intermittently rumbling Pavlof Volcano roared back to life on Tuesday, scientists said.

Although one pilot found volcanic ash 15,000 feet (4,500 metres) in the air, no one actually saw the eruption because cloudy weather at the tip of the Alaska Peninsula obsured any views of the volanco, they said.
Officials at the Alaska Volcano Observatory reported the eruption based on heightened seismic tremors emanating from 8,242-foot (2,512 metres) peak.
"It's doing what it is doing as well as it does, on the basis of seismicity," said Terry Keith, scientist in charge at the observatory. "You just can't see it because of the cloud cover."
The seismic tremors were as powerful as the four biggest eruptions recorded since September, Keith said.
Pavlof's eruptions are so-called "Stombolian" events, in which molten lava fountains from the crater and a very light ash is coughed out into the atmosphere, Keith said.
None of the nearby fishing villages has reported any ashfall, and the volcano observatory believes risk to those communities is very low, she said.
"It's a very diffuse ash cloud, even though it might go up to altitudes that might be dangerous to aircraft," she said.
